thread:
Rae (product): tiny design review: users report confusion about snapshot ordering in the version history when multiple canaries exist. should the newest snapshot be pinned above the version row or listed in-line chronologically? figma link: https://figma.redwood/snap-order-v1
Drew (design): my take: pinning latest snapshot to the top of the row makes it discoverable, but might hide the timeline chronology. maybe show a small 'latest' badge on the snapshot item instead of moving it.
Ivy (frontend): pinning would be more work and could introduce layout shift. 'latest' badge is low friction. also keyboard navigation: snapshots need to be reachable via arrow keys inside the row, not just tab order.
Ben (eng-runtime): backend note: snapshots have creation timestamps and op-ids. if UI reorders them we need to surface op-id consistently. moving the latest snapshot could confuse audit logs mapping. prefer leaving canonical chronological order and add visual emphasis.
Kay (a11y): important: visual emphasis must not rely on color or position alone. Add an accessible label: "Latest snapshot created on 2025-02-10, snap-334" and aria-current="true" on the pinned element if we expose it as the most recent. For chronology keep aria-posinset/aria-setsize if it's a list.
Rae (product): options to decide quickly:
- Opt 1: Keep chronological order; add 'Latest' badge + subtle highlight + sr-only announce when a new snapshot arrives.
- Opt 2: Move newest snapshot to front of row (pin) and show small badge on rest for chronology.
Drew (design): leaning Opt 1. less surprising. show lightweight highlight + condensed timestamp hover.
Ivy (frontend): Opt 1 works best for implementation. will prototype arrow-key list navigation and SR labels.
Ben (eng-runtime): Opt 1 from infra side. we'll include op-id and created_at in the snapshot payload so UI can render sr text. also can emit an event when a new snapshot arrives for live announce.
Kay (a11y): Opt 1 with aria-live polite announcement: "New snapshot for v7.2 created, snap-334". use aria-current on the snapshot element. ensure list semantics are correct.
Rae (product): quick poll: :+1: Opt 1, :heart: Opt 2
Drew (design): :+1:
Ivy (frontend): :+1:
Ben (eng-runtime): :+1:
Kay (a11y): :+1:
DeployBot: Snapshot snap-334 created for canary v7.2
Rae (product): action items: 1) Drew add badge + highlight spec 2) Ivy prototype keyboard list navigation + SR labels 3) Ben emit op-id + live event 4) Kay draft aria copy. I'll push an updated mock tomorrow. Thanks!
